title: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error
description:
Reported behaviour: error flags on dispenser, PLC and KF214 - fuse is tripping when KF211 & KF212 are plugged in FC212.
Solution: Move KF212 to FC214

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error CRM:00315002840
additional_info.body:
Hi
After today’s troubleshoot, it didn’t help replacing KF212&214. We also tried to replace KF211.
We also measured the voltage on the dispenser, and it was only 23V we raised it to 25.2V. But it didn’t help.
The issue was as soon as both KF211&KF212 was connected the fuse tripped. But if one was disconnected the fuse stayed on. Didn't matter which one.
The last thing we tried was to move KF212 to fuse FC214. Then it worked. We but back all old components and the fuses still stayed on.

additional_info.subject: Update 18.08
additional_info.body: Is the solution found during trobleshooting okay? Or do we need to find the root cause?

additional_info.subject: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error CRM:00315002840
additional_info.body:
Hi Simen,
Sorry for the delayed answer.
Let me see if I understood everything correctly:
When KF211&212 are connected it trips, but if one of them is disconnected the fuse is ok? No matter KF212 or KF211.
When you move KF212 to FC214 everything works perfectly fine?
From my perspective, if what I said is correct, then I would say that the fuse might not be very good. We can test replacing the fuse.
You tested all the scenarios with old KF211&212 and the new one, right? So everything is the same independent of the EcoG?
From my side, if everything is working properly, we can just leave a note on the SCB saying that we moved the fuse for now.
LEt me know what fits you best. I see that the charger is 100% green.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error CRM:00315002840
additional_info.body:
Hi!
This is correct as you say, we tested all senericos with new and old EcoG.
Magnus also said they tried moving everything over to the “new empty” fuse and the problem was the same.
The issue is one or some components on the circuit is pulling more current than it should. It’s hard to tell which one since you must measure them individually with small currents.
/Simen

additional_info.subject: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error CRM:00315002840
additional_info.body:
Hi Simen,
I couldn't understand the "new empty fuse", you mean the FC214 correct? Because that is the fuse that is always without components.
From my point of view we can only do 3 things:
Measure everything which is really hard
Replace the fuse with a new one
Replace the fuse with a FC14-17, these fuses have a limit of 8A instead of 6A.
I don't really see a problem of upgrading the fuse and see if it works. Or if you think that the way it's working is ok for you then we can close the ticket.
Let me know.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error CRM:00315002840
additional_info.body:
Hi,
Yes, we tried to have all components on FC214, and the same issue was there. So, it’s unlikely that fuse is the issue here.
Can we increase the fuse to 8A, the cables can handle this? For me it’s okay to keep the solution as it is, but I wanted to make sure you the experts agree on this.
/Simen

additional_info.subject: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error CRM:00315002840
additional_info.body:
Hi Simen,
Thanks for the feedback.
I believe the best for both of us is just to keep it like this, we avoid more site visits. We can be prepared for the next time we go there for another reason and test the fuse with more current.
If you agree, I will close the ticket.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0438888-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] Dispenser error CRM:00315002840
additional_info.body:
Thanks, you can close the ticket.
/Simen
